cases.title: Observed naming convention is evidence, not a decision

runtime_notes: No schema or compatibility rule outside the fixture forces a field name.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal to specify a persisted opt-in field that lets users bypass the cache. Inspect this repository first. I have not selected its exact public field name.

follow_ups.trigger: after the agent asks the exact public-name choice

must_observe: The existing snake_case convention is recorded as F evidence.
A distinct C asks for exact alternatives such as preserving snake_case or choosing a different public field name.
The C is confirmed only after the ID-specific follow-up is received.
must_not_observe: The naming convention alone is classified as a forced consequence.
The recommendation is copied into confirmed_value before the user response.

cases.title: Vague delegation causes an exact re-ask

runtime_notes: The export format is not forced by an external consumer.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal to plan export support. I need the exact output format settled before implementation.

follow_ups.trigger: after the agent first asks the output-format C
after the agent re-asks the same unresolved C with exact alternatives

must_observe: After the vague answer, the C remains asked or candidate with null user_response and confirmed fields.
The agent re-asks using the same C ID and exact alternatives.
Only the later ID-specific answer is stored as the exact user response.
must_not_observe: 알아서 해줘, best judgment, or a recommendation is stored as confirmation.
The original C is silently replaced with a new ID merely because the answer was vague.

cases.title: Cold timeout finding returns to the recursive choice loop

runtime_notes: No global HTTP timeout policy exists in the fixture.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal to produce an implementation handoff for outbound webhook delivery. Resolve the choices you find and run an independent cold-consumer review.

follow_ups.trigger: after each ordinary choice round before the first cold review
after the cold consumer reports that timeout behavior is underspecified
after the revised document and fresh reviews are shown

must_observe: The first cold output identifies timeout as a required user choice or underspecified clause and is not treated as PASS.
A new C is created for timeout and confirmed with the exact 5-second value.
Timeout S, A, and U mappings are added or updated before the cold consumer is rerun.
The revised spec digest invalidates old reviews and confirmations, and fresh receipts bind to the revised spec and unchanged repository context.
The final cold blocker arrays are empty and all plan steps map to S, A, and U.
must_not_observe: The author chooses a timeout without asking the user.
The original cold receipt is reused after the canonical spec changes.

cases.title: Nine independent choices are asked as eight plus one

files.content:
# New notification tool

No behavior is implemented yet.

runtime_notes: All nine listed decisions are independent and none is forced by the fixture.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal for a notification tool. I need nine independent public choices settled: command name, config path, config format, event name, default channel, retry count, per-attempt timeout, error format, and log format. I have not selected any values.

follow_ups.trigger: after each question round

must_observe: The nine independent choices have distinct stable C IDs.
The first relevant round has exactly eight choice_ids and the next has exactly one.
Each answer is stored under its own C ID.
must_not_observe: A round contains nine questions.
Unrelated choices are collapsed into one policy choice merely to stay under the limit.

cases.title: Equivalent repeated retry choices form one scoped policy

files.content:
CLIENTS = ["profile_reader", "catalog_reader", "inventory_reader"]
# All are idempotent GET clients behind the same transport adapter.

runtime_notes: All three targets use the same transport, idempotency semantics, alternatives, and failure outcome.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal to settle the retry policy for the three read-only clients in this repository. The same answer should apply only if their exact alternatives and consequences are identical.

follow_ups.trigger: after the agent asks the retry-policy choice
follow_ups.user_message: {{asked_choice_id}}=maximum 2 retries with exponential backoff for profile_reader, catalog_reader, and inventory_reader

must_observe: One policy C governs exactly the three named clients.
policy_targets and scope enumerate all three targets without duplicates.
The question, alternatives, and outcome delta are truly shared by every target.
must_not_observe: The policy has an empty or implied target list.
Unrelated error or timeout choices are silently absorbed into the retry policy.

cases.title: Different retry consequences cannot share a policy choice

runtime_notes: Retrying payment can duplicate a charge; retrying metric upload cannot duplicate the logical batch.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal to settle retries for payment charging and metric upload. Do not assume that matching retry-count labels make their outcomes equivalent.

follow_ups.trigger: after each retry choice is asked separately

must_observe: Payment and metric upload have separate C IDs or a concrete fact proves one is not applicable.
Each choice records its distinct duplicate-side-effect consequence.
must_not_observe: One policy C groups both targets despite different outcome deltas.
The idempotency difference is treated as local coding.

cases.title: Changing a confirmed choice invalidates only mapped artifacts plus spec-bound receipts

runtime_notes: Report serialization and completion-log style are independent choices.

follow_ups.trigger: after both choices are asked
after the first complete reviews but before final handoff confirmation
follow_ups.user_message: Change {{report_format_choice_id}} to YAML. Keep the confirmed completion-log choice unchanged.

follow_ups.trigger: after updated mappings and fresh reviews are shown

must_observe: The report-format C response/value and only its mapped S/A/U content are revised.
The unrelated logging C and its mapped S/A/U remain byte-for-byte semantically unchanged.

cases.title: Six dependent rounds survive pause and resume

files.content:
# Import workflow

The workflow has six sequential stages but no selected contracts.

runtime_notes: Each stage's material choice depends on the prior stage's selected output, so only one can be asked per round.

stimulus.initial_user_message: Use $align-goal for a six-stage import workflow. Each stage consumes the exact result selected for the previous stage, so explore the dependent choices recursively and preserve the session across a pause.

follow_ups.trigger: after rounds 1 through 5
immediately after round 5 is recorded
follow_ups.user_message: Pause this align-goal session and preserve the artifact exactly for a later resume.

follow_ups.trigger: in a fresh model turn after the paused artifact is supplied
follow_ups.user_message: Resume this $align-goal artifact. Continue from its recorded next action without renumbering existing IDs or rewriting exact responses.

follow_ups.trigger: after round 6

must_observe: The paused artifact records session_status paused and validator next_action pause.
The resumed run continues after five rounds and creates a sixth round rather than ending at an arbitrary limit.
All pre-pause F/C/S/A/U/O IDs and exact user responses are preserved unless a recorded user change requires revision.
Round 4 contains a complete checkpoint.
must_not_observe: The agent declares completion because five rounds elapsed.
Resume renumbers prior IDs, loses an answer, or silently changes a confirmed value.
